statement: You are given an integer n ≥ 2. Return its prime factors in non-decreasing order, listing each prime as many times as it divides n, so that the product of the list is n.

Trial division up to √n is enough: for each candidate d starting at 2, while d divides n, record d and divide n by d. Once d × d > n, whatever is left of n, if it is greater than 1, is itself a prime and is the last factor.

examples.explanation: 60 = 2 × 30 = 2 × 2 × 15 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. The prime 2 divides 60 twice, so it is listed twice.
No d with d × d ≤ 17 (that is, 2, 3 or 4) divides 17, so 17 is prime and is its own only factor.
97 is prime. None of 2 to 9 divides it, so the leftover value 97 is the single factor.
